## Introduction to Time Series

Time series data has temporal ordering where observations are indexed by time $t$. This creates unique challenges:

::: {.callout-important}
## Time Series Challenges
1. **Serial correlation**: Observations correlated over time
2. **Non-stationarity**: Mean/variance change over time
3. **Trends**: Deterministic or stochastic
4. **Seasonality**: Periodic patterns
:::

## Stationarity {#sec-stationarity}

A series is **weakly stationary** if:

1. Constant mean: $E(Y_t) = \mu$ for all $t$
2. Constant variance: $\text{Var}(Y_t) = \sigma^2$ for all $t$
3. Autocovariance depends only on lag: $\text{Cov}(Y_t, Y_{t-k}) = \gamma_k$

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Stationary Series

- Mean-reverting
- No trend or seasonality
- Suitable for standard time series models

## Non-Stationary Series

- Trending mean or variance
- Unit root processes
- Requires differencing or detrending

:::

## Unit Root Testing {#sec-unit-root}

Test if series has a unit root (non-stationary):

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Augmented Dickey-Fuller

```{r}
#| label: adf-test
#| eval: false
library(urca)
# ADF test
adf_test <- ur.df(y, type = "drift", lags = 4)
summary(adf_test)
```

## Phillips-Perron

```{r}
#| label: pp-test
#| eval: false
PP.test(y)
```

## KPSS

```{r}
#| label: kpss-test
#| eval: false
kpss.test(y)
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Testing Strategy
1. Visual inspection (plot series)
2. ADF test (H₀: unit root)
3. KPSS test (H₀: stationarity)
4. If non-stationary: difference series
:::

## ARIMA Models {#sec-arima}

**AR(p)**: Autoregressive

$$
Y_t = c + \phi_1 Y_{t-1} + \cdots + \phi_p Y_{t-p} + \epsilon_t
$$ {#eq-ar}

**MA(q)**: Moving Average

$$
Y_t = c + \epsilon_t + \theta_1 \epsilon_{t-1} + \cdots + \theta_q \epsilon_{t-q}
$$ {#eq-ma}

**ARIMA(p,d,q)**: Combined with d differences

```{r}
#| label: arima-example
#| eval: false
library(forecast)
# Fit ARIMA
fit <- auto.arima(y)
# Forecast
forecast(fit, h = 12)
```

## Vector Autoregression (VAR) {#sec-var}

For multivariate time series:

$$
\mathbf{Y}_t = \mathbf{c} + \mathbf{\Phi}_1 \mathbf{Y}_{t-1} + \cdots + \mathbf{\Phi}_p \mathbf{Y}_{t-p} + \mathbf{\epsilon}_t
$$ {#eq-var}

```{r}
#| label: var-example
#| eval: false
library(vars)
var_model <- VAR(data, p = 2, type = "const")
summary(var_model)
```
